title: Лёд для Лёвы и вызов к хозяину  (Ice for Lyova and a Summons to the Owner)

segments.t: At the end of the flashback, Nastya brings a pale, sweating Lyova a bucket of ice in the walk-in cooler after the spiked salad takes effect. Back in the present, Chef Barinov notices how pale Max looks and sends him out to the dining room to make amends with the VIP guest whose parking spot he challenged.
Alright, let's go through it step by step in English.
'The Chef told me to bring you some ice.' In Russian, the idea of 'chef' flows naturally into 'to bring' without extra filler words.
'He said you bumped yourself.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'to say' before landing on 'to hit'.
'Oh, yes.' The grammar packs 'and' and 'yes' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange. Lyova answers right away.
'I will help you with that.' The meaning hinges on 'I' working together with 'I'll help' in spoken Russian.
'I can do it myself.' Chef Viktor brings out the contrast between 'I' and 'himself' in a few short words.
'Oh come on, it is no trouble for me.' The meaning hinges on 'yes' working together with 'difficult' in spoken Russian. Chef Viktor answers right away.
'Thank you, there is no need.' Notice how Russian expresses 'thank you' and 'at' with crisp inflection rather than helper words.
'Well, how are you holding up, Lyova?' Lyova raises the pitch on 'Lyova' to turn the phrase into a direct spoken question.
'Not quite.' In Russian, the idea of 'not' flows naturally into 'at all' without extra filler words. Lyova answers right away.
'Right, we need to have a talk.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'and' before landing on 'you know'.
'You and I need to have a talk.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'for us' before landing on 'at'.
'Why are you looking so pale, huh?' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'what' and finishing on 'and'. Chef Viktor answers right away.
'Where did all the blood go from your face?' Chef Viktor brings out the contrast between 'where to' and 'whole' in a few short words. Alright, let's listen to all those lines again from the top.
When you watch Scene 10 of Episode 6, listen out for the exchange around ice for lyova and a summons to the owner — you will recognize every Russian phrase right away. See you in the next scene.
